incidents.victim: Universities and large enterprises (incl. University of Nottingham)
incidents.vector: Exploited an unauthenticated Oracle PeopleSoft PeopleTools zero-day (CVE-2026-35273, CVSS 9.8) in the Environment Management Hub for remote code execution, then used MeshCentral agents disguised as Azure services for C2, SSH credential-spraying, and zstd-compressed data exfiltration.
incidents.impact: More than 100 organizations notified (about 68% in higher education); 300+ PeopleSoft instances claimed compromised. University of Nottingham confirmed theft of 40GB+ affecting over 450,000 students and alumni; victims being extorted via the ShinyHunters leak site.

incidents.vector: The 'Outsider' phishing-kit subscription service (as low as $88/week) let customers use Gemini and other AI tools to generate fake brand sites and smishing lures impersonating tolls, deliveries, and carriers to harvest cards and credentials.
incidents.impact: FBI, Google, and Lumen dismantled the network ('Operation Ghost Hook'), which was tied to an estimated $1.9B in losses and 3.9 million stolen credit cards; admin servers, domains, a Shopify storefront, and ~$100K in wallets were seized.

incidents.vector: A 2025 breach traced to a Chinese software engineer who accessed customer data and has since left the country.
incidents.impact: South Korea's privacy regulator fined Coupang $409M (about 1.7% of 2025 sales) for the breach exposing 34 million customers' data; the company plans to appeal.

incidents.victim: Thai government healthcare agency (67 million citizens)
incidents.vector: Compromise of a government agency that manages healthcare entitlements; method not yet disclosed.
incidents.impact: Personal information of more than 67 million Thai citizens allegedly stolen, with some data posted to online criminal markets; the Thai government has launched an investigation.

incidents.vector: Compromise of the congressman's Signal messaging account; suspected Russian state hackers.
incidents.impact: The FBI notified Bacon — a staunch Ukraine supporter and Kremlin critic — that his Signal account had been breached.

incidents.vector: Cyberattack on Australia's second-largest sugar producer; details not disclosed.
incidents.impact: The company paused cane haulage and milling at two Mackay-region mills at the start of the annual crushing season, disrupting operations.

incidents.victim: Jamaica health ministry / National Health Fund
incidents.vector: Threat actor contacted the National Health Fund seeking payment not to release allegedly stolen data.
incidents.impact: The Jamaican government is investigating whether a breach occurred; the extortion attempt is active.

incidents.vector: Website defacement by a self-styled hacktivist group.
incidents.impact: The Philippines Senate website was defaced; nuisance-level disruption with no confirmed data loss.

incidents.vector: Abuse of an API bug to access data from ServiceNow customer instances; reportedly exploited since at least April.
incidents.impact: Attackers accessed customer instance data, mainly on ServiceNow's Australia platform release; the company quietly patched and notified affected customers.

incidents.victim: Conti ransomware victims (1,000+ orgs, incl. Tennessee government)
incidents.vector: Ukrainian national Oleksii Lytvynenko admitted developing malware used in Conti ransomware attacks and holding stolen data on 12 victims.
incidents.impact: Guilty plea (up to 20 years) tied to a group that hit 1,000+ victims and extorted $150M+; Tennessee attacks compromised a sheriff's department, EMS, and a local police department.

incidents.vector: Dutch financial-crime investigators arrested two operators of bulletproof hosting firms used to stage Russian cyberattacks, DDoS, and disinformation in the EU, charging them with sanctions violations.
incidents.impact: Authorities seized 800+ servers and raided data centers; the bulletproof host (a rebrand of EU-sanctioned Stark Industries) shut down, with customer data reported lost.

incidents.vector: Hackers accessed the university's CareerConnect careers portal in late May.
incidents.impact: Data of alumni, research staff, and employers was stolen from the platform that connects students and staff with recruiters and employers.

incidents.victim: Axios NPM package (100M weekly downloads) and downstream users
incidents.vector: DPRK-nexus actors (tracked as STARDUST CHOLLIMA / UNC1069) compromised the widely used Axios NPM package via a malicious postinstall dropper to poison the open-source supply chain.
incidents.impact: Likely exposed millions of downstream developers; part of a broader DPRK push into developer supply chains and trusted-access operations highlighted in new threat reporting.

incidents.victim: NûJINHA (all-female news agency, based in Turkey)
incidents.vector: Iranian-linked hackers breached the news agency's website.
incidents.impact: Attackers deleted articles, disrupted online broadcasts, and threatened to dox and harm employees.

incidents.vector: Spear-phishing operation luring WhatsApp users to click malicious links to external sites, plus creation of test accounts and groups — in violation of a 2025 U.S. court injunction.
incidents.impact: Meta said it disrupted the NSO-linked campaign and filed to hold the sanctioned spyware maker in contempt of court.

incidents.victim: U.S. law firms (incl. Weil, Gotshal & Manges)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — data extortion (Silent Ransom Group / UNC3753)
incidents.vector: Voice phishing (vishing) posing as IT support to push remote-access/RMM tools, then rapid data theft from document repositories (iManage, OneDrive); in some cases impostors entered offices in person to exfiltrate via USB.
incidents.impact: Dozens of legal, professional, and financial firms hit, often in single-day intrusions; Weil, Gotshal & Manges reportedly paid an estimated $20M ransom to prevent release of confidential client data.

incidents.victim: Instagram accounts (incl. Obama White House, U.S. Space Force)
incidents.vector: Attackers social-engineered Meta's AI support assistant into linking a new email to target accounts and triggering password resets; a VPN near the target's hometown bypassed location checks (MFA-enabled accounts were not affected).
incidents.impact: High-value Instagram accounts were briefly hijacked and defaced with pro-Iranian messages; Meta pushed an emergency patch and said no back-end database was breached.
